productTarget: Native Swift macOS cmux-like developer tool with terminal, browser, and T3 Code/Codex App-style Agent App for Codex and Claude.
hardRules: Start from zero; do not read, scan, transform, transfer, or depend on previous app data.
No fake desktop chrome and no web runtime for the app shell.
SwiftUI owns data-driven UI; AppKit owns window, responder chain, menus, focus, terminal host, complex splits, and panels.
Liquid Glass only on controls and bars, never main content.
Future mobile is not built now; desktop core must be direct-VPN-ready from day zero.
No relay, no private backend, no cloud broker, no connector id, no hosted repository mirror, no cloud command queue.
No task is done without acceptance, automated tests, E2E/proof, and fail-signal evidence.

phases.name: Phase 7 - Work Evidence And Project Actions

tasks.title: Resolve cmux Licensing Strategy
tasks.summary: Make the legal/source-reuse decision before any implementation agent uses cmux source code.
tasks.context: cmux is GPL-3.0-or-later or commercial. RemoteCode 2 can either become GPL-compatible, use a commercial license, or clean-room implement behavior without source copy.
steps: Document whether RemoteCode 2 will copy cmux code, depend on cmux packages, or only use behavioral reference.
List affected components: Bonsplit/layout, Ghostty integration, browser automation, socket/CLI API, session restore.
Write allowed and forbidden actions for implementation agents.
Update the board with the chosen constraint.
tasks.cardAcceptance: A human-readable decision exists and every later card can tell whether source reuse is allowed.
tasks.reviewChecklist: No cmux source is copied before this card is complete; the decision names license obligations and distribution impact.

verification.acceptanceCriteria: License decision names allowed source use, dependency use, notices, and distribution impact.
verification.automatedTests: Script checks source-use inventory and required third-party notice placeholders.
verification.e2eProofGate: E2E: proof gate - a dry-run implementation agent can classify cmux allowed/forbidden actions without asking.
verification.failSignal: Any cmux code copy starts before approval, or obligations remain ambiguous.

tasks.title: Choose Layout Engine Strategy
tasks.summary: Decide how RemoteCode 2 will implement workspaces, panes, splits, and surface tabs.
tasks.context: The app must behave like cmux: vertical workspaces, split panes, and horizontal surface tabs. Do not assume Bonsplit by default; choose between Bonsplit, licensed cmux layout code, and custom split-tree only after the license/package review is written.
steps: Evaluate Bonsplit, licensed cmux layout code, and a custom split-tree implementation.
Define core model types: Window, Workspace, Pane, Surface, SplitNode, PaneNode.
Specify drag/drop, keyboard focus, tab reorder, close behavior, and session snapshot needs.
Write a decision with implementation cost and risks.
tasks.cardAcceptance: A chosen layout strategy can support terminal, browser, and Agent App surfaces without per-surface special cases.
tasks.cardTests: Prototype test plan covers create split, close split, move surface, restore layout, and focus direction.

verification.acceptanceCriteria: Chosen layout model supports workspaces, split panes, tabs, focus, restore, and all surface types.
verification.automatedTests: Prototype reducer tests for split, close, move, focus, restore, and invalid layout rejection.
verification.e2eProofGate: E2E: prototype app creates terminal, browser, and Agent App placeholders in a 3-pane layout and restores after relaunch.
verification.failSignal: Any surface needs special layout handling or focus is lost after split/restore.

tasks.title: Choose Terminal Engine Strategy
tasks.summary: Prove the terminal technology before building the rest of the shell around it.
tasks.context: cmux quality depends on a real terminal. Current RemoteCode used xterm through Electrobun; RemoteCode 2 should be native.
steps: Evaluate libghostty integration, SwiftTerm, and minimal PTY+view alternatives.
Confirm build requirements for arm64 and x86_64 if universal release is required.
Define PTY lifecycle, shell selection, env injection, scrollback, copy/paste, and resize behavior.
Produce a spike app or test harness showing prompt, input, resize, close, and cleanup.
tasks.cardAcceptance: The chosen terminal can run a shell in workspace cwd and survive split/tab focus changes.
tasks.cardTests: PTY launch, command output, resize, SIGINT, close, and no orphan child process.

verification.acceptanceCriteria: Terminal engine can launch shell, render prompt, route input, resize, signal, and clean up.
verification.automatedTests: PTY lifecycle tests for cwd, output, resize, SIGINT, close, and orphan detection.
verification.e2eProofGate: E2E: spike app opens terminal, runs `pwd`, resizes pane, sends interrupt, closes, and proves no child remains.
verification.failSignal: Terminal view blanks, input leaks, resize breaks prompt, or process survives close.

tasks.title: Define Provider Runtime Contract
tasks.summary: Specify how Codex and Claude runners behave before implementing either provider.
tasks.context: Current RemoteCode has separate Codex and Claude parsers that emit one assistant event model. Swift must preserve that separation.
steps: Define `AgentProviderRunner`, `AgentRunRequest`, `AgentRunHandle`, and `AgentProviderEvent`.
Define supported provider options: model, reasoning effort, permission mode, cwd, prompt, provider thread ID.
Define cancellation semantics and process cleanup.
Define missing CLI and auth error mapping.
tasks.cardAcceptance: Codex and Claude can be implemented behind the same protocol without UI branching beyond provider-specific settings.
tasks.reviewChecklist: No UI model depends on raw Codex or Claude JSON.

verification.acceptanceCriteria: Provider contract covers Codex and Claude request fields, stream events, errors, cancellation, and missing auth.
verification.automatedTests: Contract fixture tests assert both providers map into the same normalized event schema.
verification.e2eProofGate: E2E: proof gate - fake provider run renders in Agent App timeline without provider-specific UI branches.
verification.failSignal: UI depends on raw Codex/Claude JSON or cancellation semantics differ silently.

tasks.title: Define V1 Scope And Deferred cmux Features
tasks.summary: Protect the project from scope creep while preserving a complete V1.
steps: Classify all cmux families as V1 required, V1 partial, or post-V1.
Confirm terminal, browser P0, Agent App, CLI/socket, persistence, clean first-run bootstrap, QA, signing are V1 required.
Mark SSH/cloud VM, markdown/file preview, and advanced browser P2 as post-V1 unless owner changes priority.
Add unsupported-method response rules for deferred APIs.
tasks.cardAcceptance: Every missing cmux feature has an explicit status and no agent has to infer scope.

verification.acceptanceCriteria: V1 scope lists required, partial, and deferred cmux features with unsupported-method rules.
verification.automatedTests: Scope lint verifies every feature family has status and every deferred API has an error rule.
verification.e2eProofGate: E2E: proof gate - unsupported API smoke call returns typed not-supported error with docs link.
verification.failSignal: Agent must infer scope or missing feature appears as silent no-op.

tasks.title: Create T3 Code UX Reference Spec
tasks.output: T3 UX parity spec + attribution decision
tasks.summary: Turn the T3 Code research into a precise Swift UI implementation contract before UI agents start building.
tasks.context: RemoteCode 2 must be a Swift-native app, but the Agent App and general interface should copy T3 Code's product behavior and visual structure. T3 Code is MIT; source translation requires attribution. This card prevents vague "inspired by" work.
steps: Read T3 Code README, KEYBINDINGS, LICENSE, `apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx`, `AppSidebarLayout.tsx`, `ChatView.tsx`, `chat/ChatHeader.tsx`, `chat/ChatComposer.tsx`, `chat/MessagesTimeline.tsx`, `DiffPanel.tsx`, `ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx`, `CommandPaletteResults.tsx`, and `BranchToolbar.tsx`.

Write a Swift-facing UX spec mapping each T3 Code surface to RemoteCode 2 components: sidebar, header toolbar, branch/workspace toolbar, timeline, composer, diff panel, terminal drawer, command palette, settings.

Define exact visual tokens to reproduce: dense dark surface, 1px borders, subtle muted text, compact icon buttons, small rounded controls, project/thread rows, status pills, diff additions/deletions, and bottom composer proportions.
Define what must not be copied: Electron runtime, React state architecture, fake web chrome, web-only CSS implementation details, or provider support beyond Codex and Claude for V1.
Create an attribution rule: if code or substantial UI text is translated from T3 Code, add a third-party notice and list files used.
tasks.cardAcceptance: UI agents can implement T3 Code parity from the spec without opening the T3 Code repo again, and reviewers can check every major T3 Code pattern against a written requirement.
tasks.reviewChecklist: Spec separates UX copying from source copying, includes license obligations, and preserves RemoteCode 2 native Swift/macOS constraints.

verification.acceptanceCriteria: T3 Code UX spec maps sidebar, header, timeline, composer, diff, terminal drawer, command palette, settings, and attribution.
verification.automatedTests: Spec lint checks required T3 sections, file references, license decision, and forbidden copy list.
verification.e2eProofGate: E2E: proof gate - visual checklist can evaluate a full Agent App screenshot against T3 Code structure.
verification.failSignal: Implementation agent still needs to reopen T3 Code to know core UI behavior.

tasks.title: Define SwiftUI, AppKit, And Liquid Glass UI Ownership
tasks.summary: Lock the UI implementation boundary before any visual or shell code is built.
tasks.context: RemoteCode 2 must feel like T3 Code/Codex App, but it must be a native Swift macOS app. The right architecture is not "all SwiftUI" and not "all AppKit". The boundary must be explicit so agents do not create fragile wrappers or decorative UI.
requiredDecision: Use SwiftUI for sidebar, chat timeline, composer, data lists, settings, command palette, banners, empty states, model/provider controls, and dense state-driven content.

Use AppKit for NSWindow lifecycle, responder chain, native menus, focus ownership, terminal host view/controller, complex split panes, drag/drop edge cases, file/open/save panels, and any surface that needs precise first-responder behavior.
Use Liquid Glass only for controls and bars: toolbars, compact segmented controls, icon buttons, command palette shell, modal/action surfaces, and native chrome-adjacent controls.
Do not use Liquid Glass for main content: chat transcript, timeline body, sidebar rows, diff body, terminal viewport, browser viewport, file trees, or dense repeated list cells.

Set the visual baseline as dark, dense, developer-tool, T3 Code/Codex App-like. Reject marketing-page spacing, oversized hero typography, decorative gradients, glass cards, and ornamental backgrounds.
Define the interop boundary: SwiftUI views receive state/actions; AppKit coordinators own imperative focus/window/terminal/split behavior; shared state lives outside both UI frameworks.
tasks.cardAcceptance: ADR includes a component-by-component table naming SwiftUI, AppKit, or mixed ownership, plus a "forbidden UI patterns" list that implementation agents must follow.
tasks.cardTests: Add architecture tests or lint-style checks for no fake window chrome, no Liquid Glass on main content containers, no terminal hosted purely inside unstable SwiftUI wrappers, and no command palette implemented outside the shared command model. If a rule cannot be enforced statically, add a UI/E2E assertion or review checklist item that names the exact file/component.

verification.acceptanceCriteria: ADR assigns SwiftUI/AppKit/Liquid Glass ownership per component and forbids marketing UI patterns.
verification.automatedTests: Static checks for fake chrome, Liquid Glass on main content, and terminal hosted only in SwiftUI.
verification.e2eProofGate: E2E: screenshot proves dense dark developer UI with native chrome and no decorative glass content.
verification.failSignal: Window/focus/split ownership is unclear or main content uses decorative glass.

tasks.title: Define Future Mobile Direct-VPN Mirror Contract
tasks.summary: Lock the architecture that lets a future mobile app mirror and control the desktop without a relay.
tasks.context: Current RemoteCode already exposes a local server, discovery metadata, local/VPN probing, token auth, HTTP routes, and WebSocket events. RemoteCode 2 must keep the useful direct-control idea, but start clean and remove any private-backend or relay direction.
requiredDecision: Define the future mobile promise precisely: mobile mirrors the desktop and sends commands that execute on the computer.
Declare mobile implementation out of scope for this phase, while making desktop contracts in scope.
Define direct-only networking: desktop-hosted HTTP/WebSocket over VPN or trusted LAN, no relay, no private backend, no cloud command queue, no hosted repository sync.
Define mobile-ready primitives: server identity, capabilities version, command envelope, event envelope, request id, origin client id, sequence, replay, ack, idempotency, and device trust.
List every desktop surface that must eventually be controllable: Agent App, terminal, browser, workspace/pane tabs, git actions, file context, settings subset, and command palette actions.
Write explicit non-goals: no mobile UI, no push notification feature, no APNS work, no private account system, no remote execution outside the user's computer.
tasks.cardAcceptance: Architecture agents can build desktop core and APIs without guessing how future mobile will connect, authenticate, replay state, or route commands.
tasks.reviewChecklist: ADR forbids relay/private backend design, keeps repositories and provider CLIs on the desktop, and maps mobile readiness to concrete desktop tasks and tests.

verification.acceptanceCriteria: Future mobile contract defines direct VPN/LAN transport, identity, command/event envelopes, replay, and non-goals.
verification.automatedTests: ADR lint verifies no relay/private-backend path and all required protocol fields are named.
verification.e2eProofGate: E2E: proof gate - fake future-mobile sequence diagram can execute discovery, pair, command, event replay on paper.
verification.failSignal: Any mobile path assumes a hosted relay or desktop-only private action path.

tasks.title: Implement App Lifecycle, Menus, And Native Window Shell
tasks.summary: Build the macOS shell without fake in-app window chrome.
steps: Create AppDelegate or SwiftUI App lifecycle with explicit NSWindow management.
Add native menus for app, file, edit, view, workspace, surface, window, help.
Add settings window stub and about/version metadata.
Persist and restore window bounds per release channel.
Use AppKit as the owner for NSWindow, responder chain, menu validation, first responder, focus handoff, and native window commands.

tasks.cardAcceptance: App opens one native window, uses native menu commands, and restores bounds after restart.
tasks.reviewChecklist: Desktop chrome constraint is respected; no web runtime dependency exists; AppKit owns the macOS shell behaviors that SwiftUI cannot model reliably.

verification.acceptanceCriteria: Native NSWindow, menus, responder chain, settings stub, bounds restore, and no fake chrome.
verification.automatedTests: Menu command tests, window restore tests, focus bridge tests, fake-chrome DOM/view scan.
verification.e2eProofGate: E2E: open app, use menu command, focus content, resize/relaunch, verify bounds and native chrome.

tasks.title: Implement Workspace Domain Model
tasks.summary: Create the model and reducer/store for windows, workspaces, panes, and surfaces.
steps: Define stable IDs for window, workspace, pane, split, and surface.
Define immutable actions for create, select, rename, close, split, move, reorder, focus.

Keep domain logic UI-independent.

tasks.cardTests: Create workspace, close last surface, move surface between panes, focus fallback, reorder surfaces.

verification.acceptanceCriteria: Workspace reducer preserves IDs, split invariants, selected surface, command metadata, and UI independence.
verification.automatedTests: Reducer property tests and invariant tests for create/select/close/split/move/reorder/focus.
verification.e2eProofGate: E2E: command bus drives workspace changes and UI reflects exact selected surface after reload.
verification.failSignal: Invalid split tree persists or action lacks request/origin metadata.

tasks.title: Implement T3 Code-Style Workspace Sidebar UI
tasks.summary: Build vertical workspace/project/thread navigation using T3 Code's dense sidebar as the reference.
steps: Render a T3 Code-like left rail with app identity, search row, project section header, project rows, nested thread rows, relative timestamps, status pills, and settings footer.
For each project row show icon/fallback, name, expanded state, active run indicator, latest thread preview, and git/branch metadata for git projects; show a clear "No Git" state for non-git projects.

Add search across projects and threads with keyboard navigation and command-key shortcut hint.

Support T3 Code-style compact density, muted secondary text, subtle 1px dividers, visible focus state, and responsive collapse behavior.
tasks.cardAcceptance: User can create/select/rename/archive workspaces and threads from UI and keyboard; visual structure matches T3 Code sidebar conventions while remaining native Swift/macOS.
tasks.cardTests: UI tests for search, project expand/collapse, thread selection, show-more behavior, relative timestamp updates, and keyboard focus restoration.
tasks.reviewChecklist: Text fits, no marketing/hero UI, no decorative cards inside cards, no fake macOS window controls, and T3 Code parity notes are linked in the PR/MR.

verification.acceptanceCriteria: Sidebar supports project/thread hierarchy, search, timestamps, statuses, keyboard navigation, and settings footer.
verification.automatedTests: View model tests for filtering, sorting, expand/collapse, rename/archive, timestamp updates.
verification.e2eProofGate: E2E: create projects/threads, search/select/show-more, navigate by keyboard, compare screenshot to T3 sidebar.

tasks.title: Implement Pane Split And Surface Tab UI
tasks.summary: Expose the cmux-like work area where all surface types live.
steps: Render split tree with resizable dividers.
Render horizontal surface tabs per pane with icon, title, dirty/unread state, close button, and selected state.
Add commands for split right/down, focus directionally, close surface, close pane, equalize splits.
Route selected surface to SurfaceRenderer by type.
Use AppKit for complex split-pane mechanics when SwiftUI cannot provide stable drag, focus, sizing, and first-responder behavior.
Use SwiftUI for pane tab labels, surface metadata, and declarative state display inside the AppKit-owned split structure.
tasks.cardAcceptance: Placeholder terminal/browser/agent surfaces can be created, switched, split, and closed.
tasks.cardTests: UI test for 3-surface split layout and focus direction.

verification.acceptanceCriteria: Pane/tab UI can create, switch, split, close, move, and focus all placeholder surfaces.
verification.automatedTests: Layout reducer tests, split geometry tests, tab lifecycle tests, focus direction tests.
verification.e2eProofGate: E2E: build terminal left, Agent App top-right, browser bottom-right; switch tabs and close panes safely.

tasks.title: Implement T3 Code-Style Command Palette And Keybindings
tasks.summary: Add T3 Code-like keyboard-first access to commands, projects, threads, terminal actions, and scripts.
steps: Define command contribution model with id, title, subtitle/description, icon, keywords, shortcut command, timestamp/trailing metadata, availability predicate, and action.

Register commands for search/open project, search/open thread, new chat/thread, new local/worktree thread, split terminal, new terminal, close terminal, toggle terminal, toggle diff, open editor, run project script, workspace/surface actions, browser actions, and Agent App actions.

Implement T3 Code-compatible keybinding concepts: shortcut string, command id, nullable boolean `when` expression, contexts for terminal focus/open state, invalid-rule warnings, and last matching rule wins.
Use T3 Code default shortcuts as the reference: terminal toggle, terminal split/new/close, command palette toggle, new chat, new local chat, open favorite editor, and script run commands.
Add fuzzy search, grouped results, disabled rows, keyboard highlight, enter to run, escape to close, submenu affordance, and shortcut labels.
Ensure palette focus does not leak keystrokes to terminal, browser, or composer surfaces.
tasks.cardAcceptance: Command palette can create/open a T3 Code-style Agent App thread, split/toggle terminal, open project/editor, and show grouped results with shortcuts.
tasks.cardTests: Unit tests for keybinding parsing, `when` evaluation, last-rule precedence, command filtering, disabled items, and focus isolation; UI tests for keyboard navigation and execution.

verification.automatedTests: Parser, precedence, availability, fuzzy-search, disabled-row, and focus-isolation tests.
verification.e2eProofGate: E2E: open palette, create Agent App thread, split terminal, toggle diff, and verify no keystrokes leak.

tasks.title: Implement SQLite Persistence Foundation
tasks.summary: Create the database layer, schema versioning, and repositories used by all later features.
steps: Choose and configure GRDB or direct SQLite based on the architecture decision.
Create versioned schema steps for projects, agent threads, messages, runs, events, snapshots, settings, and session snapshots.
Implement repository protocols and concrete SQLite repositories.
Add in-memory/test database setup.
Ensure app data directories differ for debug, canary, and stable.

tasks.title: Implement Direct-VPN Desktop API Foundation
tasks.summary: Create the desktop-hosted HTTP/WebSocket foundation that a future mobile app will use over VPN.
tasks.hardRule: This API is direct desktop access only. Do not add hosted relay, private backend forwarding, connector ids, cloud command queues, or repository mirroring.
steps: Create a desktop HTTP server owned by the macOS app, disabled for non-loopback access until the user explicitly enables VPN/LAN access.
Add `/v1/discovery` with server id, app version, capabilities version, auth mode, enabled transports, host/port, VPN/LAN connect hints, and health status.
Add `/v1/capabilities` covering available surfaces, command versions, provider availability, terminal/browser support, git support, and feature flags.
Add direct WebSocket endpoint `/v1/ws` with authenticated join/leave, ping/pong, and protocol-version negotiation.
Add mDNS or QR/manual-connect metadata only when it points to direct desktop addresses.
Keep API handlers thin: they validate auth and protocol, then call the shared command bus used by desktop UI and CLI.

verification.e2eProofGate: E2E: fake client connects over loopback/VPN-enabled path, reads capabilities, joins WebSocket, receives event.
verification.failSignal: API contains relay/private-backend fields or listens beyond loopback without opt-in.

Add remote access settings: disabled by default, loopback-only default, explicit VPN/LAN enablement, visible host/port, rotate credentials, revoke device, and audit log viewer.
Store secrets in Keychain or equivalent secure storage; never store production tokens in plain SQLite.
Rate-limit auth failures and log denied attempts without leaking tokens or prompts.
Document that the mobile app is not built yet; settings exist to validate and operate the desktop contract safely.
tasks.cardAcceptance: Direct remote access cannot be enabled accidentally, every trusted device can be revoked, and no production default token exists.

Persist enough event history to replay workspace and active-thread state for reconnecting future mobile clients.
Implement WebSocket subscription by scope: app, workspace, Agent App thread, terminal session, browser surface, and git status.
Implement last-sequence replay, ack, duplicate request suppression, backpressure limits, and deterministic error events.
Route desktop UI actions through this bus instead of private view-only callbacks so mobile parity is architectural, not bolted on later.
tasks.cardAcceptance: A fake remote client can reconnect with last sequence and receive exactly the missed events, while duplicate commands do not execute twice.

verification.e2eProofGate: E2E: fake mobile disconnects, desktop changes state, reconnects with last sequence, receives missed events once.

Surface contracts cover Agent App, terminal, browser, git/files, workspace/panes, and remote-access settings.
